text:
hana-sales: Beta customer on Dedicated POC hit intermittent 5xxs during scheduled load test. They said errors started around 2:10pm and are mostly 500/502. Can we triage?
liam-support: Copy. Any request IDs or sample responses? Are they using our SDK or direct API?
beta-customer: sending sample log snippets (sanitized):
```
2026-04-02T14:10:12Z ERR req=zzz111 backend_error=502 proxy=upstream_unavailable
2026-04-02T14:10:14Z ERR req=zzz112 service=runtime error=internal_server_error queue_ms=1800
```
anya-se: Thanks. Quick glance at runtime shows "capacity_throttle" and queue climb before 5xxs. Autoscaler created scale event but pods came up ~70s after initial spike.
tom-eng: If autoscaler lag is the culprit we can do three things fast: 1) temporary manual scale to handle peak, 2) enable lightweight fallback (smaller model) for the customer traffic shape, 3) apply client-side rate shaping to smooth ramp.
hana-sales: Customer asked how long a manual scale takes and cost impact for a 2hr window.
liam-support: Manual scale: adding X GPUs typically takes ~3-5mins for allocation + pod spin. Cost: approx $X/hour per GPU. I'll get exact numbers from billing.
infra-bot: event: autoscaler_detected_spike id=evt-902 created=2026-04-02T14:11:20Z scaled_from=2 scaled_to=6 reason=throughput_spike
anya-se: Note autoscaler cooldown is 90s and default threshold is 75%. For a POC with synthetic ramps we usually recommend cooldown 30s + threshold 60% or fallback.
liam-support: For troubleshooting, can someone run these checks and paste outputs?
- runtime logs grep "capacity_throttle" for last 30m
- k8s events for custom scaler
- queue metrics from /api/metrics?window=30m

tom-eng: I'll pull logs:
```
rg "capacity_throttle" /mnt/runtime/logs/*.log | tail -n 200
kubectl -n inference get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 50
```
liam-support: Also, capture one failing request_id so we can trace through scheduler -> runtime -> worker.
beta-customer: sending failing request id zzz112. They also noted increased token limits during test (max_tokens=2048).
anya-se: High max_tokens increases compute per request — that combined with concurrent ramp could saturate workers faster. Recommend reducing max_tokens to 512 for stress window.
tom-eng: Proposed quick mitigation checklist to send to customer:
- reduce max_tokens to 512
- apply client ramp: start 10rps, increase 10rps every 15s
- enable fallback_variant: rwd-3b for 20% of requests during ramp
- ask support to manual-scale to 8 GPUs for 2hrs (rollback after test)
- enable prefix_cache if repeated prompts
hana-sales: I'll share that and ask for a 2hr maintenance/test window.
liam-support: I'll open SUP-2026-CTL-117 and attach timeline + logs.
anya-se: I'll prepare a one-click config patch they can paste to console to enable fallback and change autoscaler parameters. Snippet below:
```
routing:
  fallback_variant: rwd-3b
  fallback_pct: 0.2
autoscaler:
  scale_up_cooldown: 30s
  cpu_threshold: 60
```
liam-support: Customer worried about SLA impact and error attribution — we should document timeline and correlate autoscaler events to errors.
tom-eng: If errors persist after these mitigations we may need an emergency scheduler patch to reduce cold-start latency for new workers. Keep infra on standby.
beta-customer: Applying client-side smoothing now and reducing max_tokens. We'll run another ramp in ~20m and report back. Thanks for the checklist.
hana-sales: Perfect, I'll coordinate the window and send cost estimate when billing responds. Keep this thread for updates. :white_check_mark:
